gurus.name: Guru Nanak Dev Ji
gurus.born: Rai Bhoi di Talwandi, now Nankana Sahib, in 1469.
facts: Travelled far and wide on long journeys (udasis) to share his message.
Taught that there is one God, and that all people are equal.
Founded the town of Kartarpur, where everyone worked, prayed and ate together.

gurus.name: Guru Angad Dev Ji
gurus.born: Matte di Sarai, near Muktsar, in 1504.
facts: Gave the Gurmukhi script the shape we learn today.
Opened schools so children could learn to read and write.
With Mata Khivi Ji, grew the langar so everyone could eat together.
Encouraged healthy bodies with exercise and wrestling.

gurus.name: Guru Amar Das Ji
facts: Asked every visitor to sit together and eat in langar first — rich or poor, side by side (pangat).
Built the baoli (step-well) at Goindval Sahib.
Spoke up for women and taught that they are equal.

gurus.name: Guru Ram Das Ji
facts: Founded the city of Ramdaspur, which we now call Amritsar.
Began digging the holy sarovar (pool) at Amritsar.
Wrote the Laavan, the four hymns sung at a Sikh wedding.

gurus.name: Guru Arjan Dev Ji
facts: Built Sri Harmandir Sahib, with four doors open to everyone.
Gathered the Gurus' bani into the Adi Granth in 1604.
Wrote Sukhmani Sahib, the Prayer of Peace.
Gave his life in 1606 — the first Sikh shaheed.

gurus.name: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji
gurus.born: Guru ki Wadali, near Amritsar, in 1595.
facts: Wore two swords, Miri and Piri — caring for the world and for the spirit.
Built the Akal Takht in Amritsar.
Freed 52 kings from Gwalior Fort, remembered on Bandi Chhor Divas.

gurus.name: Guru Har Rai Ji
facts: Loved nature and kept gardens full of plants and animals.
Ran a place where sick people were given free medicine.
Taught everyone to be gentle with all living things.

gurus.name: Guru Har Krishan Ji
facts: Became Guru when he was only five years old.
In Delhi, cared for people who were ill during an epidemic.
Gurdwara Bangla Sahib stands where he stayed in Delhi.

gurus.name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
facts: Founded the town that became Anandpur Sahib.
Stood up for people's freedom to follow their own faith.
Gave his life in Delhi in 1675; Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib marks the place.
His bani is in Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

gurus.name: Guru Gobind Singh Ji
facts: Created the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib on Vaisakhi, 1699.
Was a poet and wrote many banis.
In 1708 at Nanded, made Guru Granth Sahib Ji the eternal Guru.

gurus.name: Guru Granth Sahib Ji
gurus.born: First gathered as the Adi Granth by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in 1604.
facts: Holds the bani of six Gurus and of holy people (Bhagats) from different faiths.
Written in Gurmukhi, with 1430 pages called angs.
Guru Gobind Singh Ji gave it the Guruship in 1708.
Sikhs bow to Guru Granth Sahib Ji as their living Guru.

fiveKs.meaning: Uncut hair — accepting the body as God made it
A small wooden comb — keeping clean and tidy
A steel bracelet — a reminder to do good
A reminder to stand up for what is right

gurdwaras.name: Sri Harmandir Sahib
about: Built by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in the middle of the sarovar started by Guru Ram Das Ji.
It has four doors, showing it is open to people from every direction and every background.
Its langar serves free meals to many thousands of people every day.

gurdwaras.name: Sri Akal Takht Sahib
about: Built by Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, facing Sri Harmandir Sahib.
The first of the five Takhts — seats of Sikh authority.

gurdwaras.name: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib
about: Stands where Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa on Vaisakhi, 1699.
Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

gurdwaras.name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
about: Guru Gobind Singh Ji stayed here, and the full Guru Granth Sahib was prepared here.
It is one of the five Takhts.

gurdwaras.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
about: Marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1666.
It is one of the five Takhts.

gurdwaras.name: Takht Sri Hazur Sahib
about: Here Guru Gobind Singh Ji made Guru Granth Sahib Ji the eternal Guru in 1708.
It is one of the five Takhts.

gurdwaras.name: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib
about: Guru Har Krishan Ji stayed here and cared for sick people.
Visitors still take water from its sarovar.

gurdwaras.name: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib
about: Marks where Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji gave his life in 1675 for freedom of faith.

gurdwaras.name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan
about: Marks the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji in 1469.

gurdwaras.name: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur
about: Guru Nanak Dev Ji lived his last years here, farming and sharing with everyone.
